newsitem.title: UK: BA still negotiating on American deal with UK.
newsitem.headline: BA still negotiating on American deal with UK.

text.p: British Airways Plc confirmed on Friday it has not yet agreed terms with Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) for getting UK clearance for its proposed alliance with American Airlines.
"We are still in discussions with the OFT," said a spokeswoman. "There are still a number of issues outstanding," she said.
The OFT said on Friday it had not yet reported back to Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang, who would then give the final ruling.
This meant there was still no deal. "If the advice has not yet gone over (to Lang) then we will still be negotiating," an official at the OFT said.

The deal is also being examined by regulators in the U.S. and the European Commission and requires Britain and the U.S. to agree an "open skies" airlines trade pact to open up the transatlantic market.
But everything else in the process hinges on the long awaited British ruling.

Lang announced initial proposals in December for clearing the deal, provided that BA and American could reach agreement with the OFT on satisfactory conditions. In particular Lang had proposed that BA and American should "release" up to 168 weekly runway slots at London Heathrow to make more room for transatlantic competition. and invited other airlines an interested parties to comment to the OFT.
The key issue of whether BA should be allowed to sell the slots or give them up for free was left open to further negotiations with the OFT, and to consultations with rival airlines.
Rival airlines have said more concessions need to be made at Heathrow if BA and American are to be prevented from dominating the British transatlantic market with 62 percent of all current capacity.
Access to Heathrow is also the key issue in the open skies negotiations which were adjourned last week.
But British Airways Plc declined to comment on Friday on a report that its chief executive has asked Britain to break the regulatory logjam.

The Independent newspaper had said Robert Ayling met with Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine in an effort to try and speed the process up, on fears that a change in government might jeopardise the whole deal.
Opinion polls make the opposition Labour Party a strong favourite to win the election, due to be held by mid-May.
A spokesman said the airline would neither confirm or deny whether any talks took place.
"We meet people of all political persuasions all the time to talk about a great number of issues," he said.
